chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar all together, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a girl who has not attained puberty: when is it incumbent on her to cover her head from the one with whom she does not share any relation? and when is it obligatory on her to veil her head fully in the prayer? He said: She does not cover her head until the prayer starts becoming prohibited on her.

key_terms.تَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهَا الصَّلَاة: prayer becomes prohibited on her (due to menstruation)
key_terms.مَحْرَم: mahram (close relative with whom marriage is prohibited)

ai.seo_question: When does a girl become obligated to cover her head in Islam according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of head covering (hijab) for girls is contingent upon the onset of menstruation (hayd), which serves as the primary marker of legal maturity (bulugh) in this context. This ruling distinguishes between general childhood modesty and the binding religious duty, linking the hijab requirement directly to the validity of prayer rather than a fixed chronological age. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that major acts of worship and their associated veiling requirements are predicated on the physiological signs of puberty.
